memory_candidates.content: When a verify-deploy.sh gate reports a per-gate wrapper TIMEOUT (exit 124) under concurrent-batch load, re-run the SAME underlying check standalone outside the timeout wrapper (e.g. bash .claude/scripts/validate-state.sh --deep specs/state.json) before concluding the task introduced a regression. The standalone run often completes well under the wrapper's timeout and reveals the real (often pre-existing) content finding, letting you distinguish a resource-contention artifact from an actual defect.

A local foreground command that plausibly exceeds the harness Bash tool's default 120000ms timeout gets silently auto-backgrounded. Recover with the bounded-build-waiter idiom: detach via nohup + '&', capture pid=$!, then poll liveness in one Bash call with 'while kill -0 "$pid"; do sleep N; done' bounded by a large outer timeout parameter (up to 600000ms) and an inner elapsed-time break -- never a raw inner `timeout N cmd` piped through tail, since that SIGTERMs the command at N seconds even though the harness's own foreground ceiling is separate and larger.
